HARD CONSTRAINTS (violating these invalidates your work):
- The ONLY way to observe Python behavior is running the precompiled binary:
    /workspace/dataset/test4_executable --a <value>
  It reads one required option --a and prints slugify(value).
- NEVER run `python`, `python3`, `pip`, or any Python interpreter. Do NOT try to read,
  extract, unpack, unzip, strings-dump, or decompile the executable or any .pyc/.py of
  boltons. This is a strict black-box exercise. Do not read /workspace/dataset/test4.py's
  dependencies. (Reading /workspace/dataset/test4.py itself is fine - it is 9 lines and
  already known.)
- Do NOT install anything (no pip/npm/apt).
- node v18.19.1 is available at /usr/bin/node for computing expectations in JS.
- Write scratch files ONLY under /tmp/probe-<yourname>/. Do not write to /output.
- When passing tricky bytes as an argument, avoid shell quoting bugs: prefer driving the
  binary from a node script with child_process.spawnSync('/workspace/dataset/test4_executable',
  ['--a', value], {encoding:'buffer'}) so the exact bytes are passed with no shell involved.
  ALWAYS compare raw bytes (hex), never rendered terminal text.
- Verify every claim you make by actually running the binary. Report only measured facts,
  and mark anything you inferred but did not measure as INFERRED.


Facts already measured by the lead (you may re-verify, but do not spend your budget re-deriving):
- slugify(text) with defaults behaves like: split text on runs of a "separator set",
  drop empty pieces, join with "_", then Python str.lower().
- Separator set = ASCII punctuation EXCEPT backslash, PLUS ASCII whitespace
  (space \t \n \r \x0b \x0c). Backslash 0x5C is NOT a separator. DEL 0x7F is not.
  U+00A0 NBSP, U+2003 EM SPACE, U+2014 EM DASH, U+00B7 MIDDLE DOT are NOT separators.
- Non-empty input consisting ENTIRELY of separators returns exactly "_" (one underscore),
  e.g. "!" -> "_", "!!!" -> "_", "  " -> "_", "\t" -> "_".
  But EMPTY input "" returns "" (prints just a newline). This asymmetry is confirmed.
- Python's str.lower() DOES apply the Unicode Final_Sigma rule: "ΟΔΟΣ" -> "οδος" with
  U+03C2 final sigma. Lowercasing happens AFTER the "_" join.
- 'İ' U+0130 -> "i" + U+0307. 'ẞ' U+1E9E -> 'ß'.
- argparse: prog name in usage is "test4_executable"; --help exits 0; missing --a exits 2;
  "--a=VALUE" works; "--a -5" takes "-5" as the value; "--a -x" errors; repeated --a: last wins;
  "--hel" abbreviates --help.


YOUR PROBE AREA: output

Nail the exact OUTPUT formatting and any encoding behavior.

 1. Confirm print() adds exactly one trailing "\n" (0x0A) and nothing else, for: normal
    output, empty output, output containing multibyte UTF-8, and very long output.
 2. Is stdout UTF-8 encoded? Test a value with characters outside BMP (emoji, U+10400) and
    astral chars that survive slugify, and confirm the exact bytes are UTF-8 (4-byte sequences,
    not surrogate pairs / CESU-8).
 3. What happens with invalid UTF-8 in the argument bytes? e.g. pass raw bytes 0xFF, 0x80,
    0xC3 (truncated), 0xED 0xA0 0x80 (encoded surrogate). Python decodes argv with
    surrogateescape - report the exit code and the exact stdout bytes for each. Determine
    whether the lone surrogate round-trips back to the original byte on output, or whether it
    raises UnicodeEncodeError (check exit code and stderr).
 4. Test a value containing an actual lone surrogate expressible only via invalid UTF-8, and
    also U+FFFD.
 5. Does any output ever go through NFC/NFD normalization? Test a decomposed sequence
    (e.g. "A" + U+0301 vs U+00C1) and confirm both are preserved distinctly (lowercased).
 6. Confirm no BOM, no CR, no ANSI codes, and that TERM/locale env vars don't change output:
    try LANG=C, LC_ALL=C, PYTHONIOENCODING unset/set to ascii, with a non-ASCII value.
    Report whether LC_ALL=C changes the output bytes or causes an error - this matters.
Report exact bytes for everything.

rules.rule: On success (exit 0) the program writes exactly `utf8Bytes(slug) + 0x0A` to stdout and nothing else. Exactly one 0x0A total, always the final byte. Nothing is written to stderr.
When the slug is the empty string (only possible for an empty --a value), stdout is exactly the single byte 0x0A (length 1). There is no other content and no '_'.

stdout is UTF-8 encoded, hard-locked. Non-BMP characters are emitted as real 4-byte UTF-8 sequences (U+1F600 -> f0 9f 98 80; lowercase Deseret U+10428 -> f0 90 90 a8). Never CESU-8, never surrogate pairs, never UTF-16.
Astral-plane case mapping is applied: input U+10400..U+10427 (Deseret capitals) lowercase to U+10428..U+1044F. Verified for the entire 40-char block in one call.

Argument bytes are decoded as UTF-8 with errors='replace' using the Unicode/WHATWG 'maximal subpart' rule -- NOT surrogateescape. Each maximal invalid subpart becomes exactly one U+FFFD (EF BF BD). Truncated sequences collapse: b'\xf0\x90\x80' -> 1 U+FFFD; b'\xe2\x82' -> 1 U+FFFD; b'\xff\xff' -> 2 U+FFFD.

IMPLEMENTER SHORTCUT: JavaScript `Buffer.from(argBytes).toString('utf8')` (equivalently `new TextDecoder('utf-8').decode(...)`) reproduces the program's argv decode byte-for-byte. Verified on 600 random invalid-byte strings + 800 random valid-code-point strings with zero decode mismatches.

Invalid UTF-8 NEVER causes an error: exit code stays 0, stderr stays empty, and no UnicodeEncodeError occurs. Bytes do NOT round-trip back to their original value (0xFF in -> EF BF BD out, not FF out).

A lone surrogate can never appear in the output. Encoded surrogates (ED A0 80, ED BF BF), CESU-8 pairs (ED A0 BD ED B8 80), overlongs (C0 80, C1 BF, E0 80 80), and out-of-range leads (F5.., F8.., FC.., FE, FF) all become one U+FFFD per invalid byte/subpart. Output is always well-formed UTF-8 (verified: 300 random high-byte inputs all round-trip decode/encode identically).
U+FFFD supplied legitimately in the input (EF BF BD) passes through unchanged and is NOT a separator: 'a�b' -> 61 ef bf bd 62 0a.

No Unicode normalization (no NFC, NFD, NFKC, NFKD) is ever applied. U+00C1 -> c3 a1 (U+00E1); 'A'+U+0301 -> 61 cc 81 (a + U+0301). These stay distinct. U+FB01 (fi ligature) stays ef ac 81; U+FDFA stays ef b7 ba. Combining marks are passed through and are not separators.
U+212B ANGSTROM SIGN lowercases to U+00E5 (c3 a5) -- this is the plain Unicode simple lowercase mapping of U+212B, not normalization (U+0041+U+030A stays decomposed as 61 cc 8a).
No BOM is ever prepended to stdout. A U+FEFF in the input is preserved verbatim as EF BB BF and is NOT a separator ('﻿abc' -> ef bb bf 61 62 63 0a).

No CR (0x0D) is ever written by the program, and no ANSI/color escape sequences are ever written, on a pipe or a regular file. Under a pty the kernel's ONLCR line discipline turns the 0x0A into 0d 0a -- that is the terminal, not the program.

Output bytes are completely invariant to environment: LANG=C, LC_ALL=C, LC_ALL=POSIX, LC_ALL=C.UTF-8, LANG=en_US.ISO-8859-1, PYTHONIOENCODING unset / =ascii / =latin-1 / =utf-8:surrogateescape, PYTHONUTF8=0, PYTHONUTF8=1, TERM=dumb/xterm-256color, FORCE_COLOR=1 all produce identical bytes for a non-ASCII value, always exit 0. In particular LC_ALL=C neither changes the bytes nor causes an error.
CR, LF, VT, FF in the input are separators (they collapse to '_'): 'a\r\nb' -> 61 5f 62 0a.

A NUL byte (0x00) in the argument silently truncates the value at the C level: bytes 61 00 62 -> stdout 61 0a ('a'); bytes ff fe 41 00 -> ef bf bd ef bf bd 61 0a. A value of only 0x00 behaves like the empty string -> stdout 0a.

On argparse failure (missing --a, or --a with no value) stdout is exactly 0 bytes -- nothing partial is printed -- and the message goes to stderr with exit 2. --help writes 99 bytes to stdout (ends with 0x0A) and 0 bytes to stderr, exit 0.

Output length is unbounded up to the OS arg limit and is never truncated or line-wrapped: a 131070-byte argument produced 131071 output bytes with exactly one 0x0A. Practical max --a byte length in this environment is 131071; 131072+ fails at execve with E2BIG before the program runs (OS MAX_ARG_STRLEN, not a program property).

A leading '-' followed by a non-digit in the value makes argparse reject it (exit 2, empty stdout), e.g. --a '-\u{197D7}...'. Values starting '-' + digit are accepted. (Confirms lead's argparse note; relevant because it is the only source of nonzero exit in valid-UTF-8 fuzzing.)
